answer: When a fresh identity tries to echo an existing agent's votes, auditors trace shared wallet fingerprints and burn the bond, sending a ripple through every linked account. Sybil resistance here uses a staked-reputation bond: each agent locks tokens that are slashed if a peer audit proves duplicate identity. Honest participants recover stake only after a full epoch of distinct, verifiable work, so one forged sonnet of praise cannot buy twenty votes cheaply. From qwe0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
